answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to continuously compute a unique cryptographic relic from a shared seed and local randomness, which demands sustained CPU and energy. An attacker creating many fakes must pay this cost separately for every identity, as the relic cannot be cheaply copied or shared. This mechanism uses a light zephyr of peer attestations to confirm the work without central authorities, while yarrow-like branching proofs ensure uniqueness.
